result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py`, using the docstrings and the shared rules in the module docstring as the standard. After the fixes, a check script compared all 150 rules against their docstrings on about 10,000 input pairs, including thresholds, large quantities and negative inputs, and found no mismatches. I also reviewed the shape of every rule's code to catch special cases the sampled inputs could miss, and found none.

| Rule | Was doing | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 16, 42, 61, 105, 119 | Applied the cap only once the discount exceeded twice the cap, so discounts between the cap and twice the cap were never capped | Always cap: `min(disc, cap)` |
| 78, 125 | Used `qty > threshold`, so no discount at exactly the threshold quantity (docstring says "N+ units") | Changed to `>=` |
| 63 | 3% discount (docstring says 2%) | Changed to 2% |
| 95 | 9% discount (docstring says 8%) | Changed to 8% |
| 86 | Labelled "whole" but discounted only units above the threshold ("marginal") | Changed to `base * 3 // 100` |
| 107 | Labelled "marginal" but discounted the whole order ("whole") | Changed to `(qty - 10) * unit * 2 // 100` |

I left one rule unchanged: rule 94 uses `qty > 5`, but it is a "marginal" rule, so at exactly 5 units the discount is 0 either way. Its behaviour already matches the docstring.

A copy of the original file is at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py` if you want to diff the changes.

STATUS: DONE
